cards.claim: Cyclical learning rate (CLR) with large maximum learning rate achieves higher CIFAR-10 accuracy than standard training in substantially fewer iterations
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10 dataset, ResNet-56 architecture, 50,000 training samples, cyclical learning rate (0.1-3.0 range), cyclical momentum 0.95, batch normalization momentum reduced to 0.95
cards.effect: 92.4% accuracy in ~10,000 iterations vs 91.2% in ~80,000 iterations (1.2 percentage point improvement, ~8x speedup)
cards.evidence: Experimental results reported in Figure 1(a) and Table 1
cards.quote: Piecewise constant training reaches a peak accuracy of 91.2% after approximately 80,000 iterations, while the super-convergence method reaches a higher accuracy (92.4%) after only 10,000 iterations.

cards.claim: CLR with cyclical momentum improves CIFAR-10 accuracy substantially when training data is limited (10,000-40,000 samples), with larger improvements for smaller datasets
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10, ResNet-56, variable training set sizes (10K-40K samples), CLR (0.1-3), cyclical momentum 0.95, 10,000 total iterations, reduced BN momentum (0.95 vs 0.999)
cards.effect: With 10,000 training samples: 80.6% (CLR) vs 71.4% (standard training) = 9.2 percentage point improvement. With 20,000 samples: 87.9% vs 82.7% = 5.2 point improvement. With 40,000 samples: 91.1% vs 89.1% = 2.0 point improvement.
cards.evidence: Table 1 comparing CLR vs piecewise constant learning rate across different training set sizes, plus explicit statement in text
cards.quote: super-convergence test accuracy is 1.2%, 5.2%, and 9.2% better for 50,000, 20,000, and 10,000 training cases, respectively.

cards.claim: Batch normalization momentum must be reduced (from 0.999 to 0.95) when using large cyclical learning rates for proper regularization balance
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10, ResNet-56, using CLR with learning rates 0.1-3.0, requires reduction of all forms of regularization
cards.effect: Enables use of large learning rates without divergence; part of maintaining optimal regularization balance for super-convergence
cards.evidence: Table 1 explicitly shows BN MAF (batch normalization momentum) parameter changes: 0.999 for standard training vs 0.95 for CLR; theoretical discussion in paper
cards.quote: A primary insight that allows super-convergence training is that large learning rates regularize the training, hence requiring a reduction of all other forms of regularization in order to preserve an optimal regularization balance.

cards.claim: 1cycle learning rate policy achieves higher CIFAR-100 test accuracy than step learning rate policy in 25 epochs (relevant comparison point even if exceeds ≤15 epoch budget)
cards.conditions: CIFAR-100 dataset, ResNet-56 architecture, 1cycle policy with CLR 0.1-0.5 range, cyclical momentum 0.95-0.85, 25 epochs total
cards.effect: Significantly higher accuracy at 25 epochs than standard step learning rate policy achieves in 100+ epochs
cards.evidence: Table 2 results for CIFAR-100 and explicit statement in text
cards.quote: The training results from the 1cycle learning rate policy are significantly higher than the results from the step learning rate policy and the number of epochs required for training is greatly reduced (i.e., at only 25 epochs the accuracy is higher than any with a step learning rate policy).

cards.claim: Large learning rates with cyclical annealing achieve CIFAR-10 accuracy improvements with reduced iteration count across a range of stepsize values
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10, ResNet-56, cyclical learning rate modified to 1cycle policy, learning rate varies from 0.1 to 3.0, stepsize varied (2,000 to 20,000 iterations total)
cards.effect: Final accuracy improves from 89.7% (2,000 iterations) to 92.1% (6,000 iterations) to 92.7% (20,000 iterations), with 6,000 iterations achieving higher accuracy (92.1%) than standard training (91.2%)
cards.evidence: Figure 1(b) with multiple stepsize comparisons showing robustness of method
cards.quote: In addition, as the total number of iterations increases from 2,000 to 20,000, the final accuracy improves from 89.7% to 92.7%. This modified learning rate schedule achieves a higher final test accuracy (92.1%) than typical training (91.2%) after only 6,000 iterations.
